inputs.new_evidence: Context: mneme is a Plexus RPC server implementing the BLF (Bayesian Linguistic Forecaster) framework from Murphy 2026 (arXiv 2604.18576). The paper claims SOTA on ForecastBench, beating GPT-5, Grok 4.20, and Foresight-32B. The paper headline figure shows LOO-shrinkage (leave-one-out) consistently outperforming plain mean across Metaculus Baseline Score, Brier Score, and Brier Index. Our current implementation diverges: we shrink trial probabilities in logit space toward a fixed prior of 0.5 with lambda=0.2 instead of LOO-shrinkage. Question: If we replace fixed-prior shrinkage with LOO-shrinkage as described in the paper, will the mean Brier score on a 50-question sample of ForecastBench improve by more than 0.005? Research the paper if needed.
